rationale: Evidence from iteration 6 (score 619.4): the oval completes 20/20 (2.07 s, rms 0.014), and the s-bend completes 18/20 (progress 0.96, 2.68 s). Slalom is the failure: 0/20 finish, progress 0.17, about one line-loss event per run, and max_error at the 0.06 m off-track floor with rms about 0.027. Oscillation on slalom is low (0.21), so the robot is not jittering. It is responding too slowly to the alternating weaves and drifting out. The s-bend result shows that the speed and damping change (0.85 to 0.75, kd 0.7 to 0.8) fixed the bend slip, but slalom barely moved (0.165 to 0.167 progress). That suggests the limit on slalom is steering authority and response, not speed. Changes: kp 5.3 to 6.5 for a stronger correction on each weave, and kd 0.8 to 1.0 to keep that gain damped. Geometry, sensor span, sensor weights, base_speed, ki and line_loss stay unchanged, so this iteration isolates the gain effect. Hypotheses: (a) slalom progress rises above 0.4 with the higher kp; (b) the oval still finishes in at least 90% of trials, with steering_oscillation under about 0.35 thanks to the extra kd; (c) line_loss_events on slalom fall below 0.5. Risk: the higher gain may oscillate on the oval. If oscillation exceeds 0.35 or the oval fails, the next step is kd up before kp is reduced. If slalom still exits with progress flat, the next lever is sensor_size 0.016 for wider tape coverage on sharp weaves.
